name: Hamburg, Germany

bremen-far.name: Bremen

sights.name: Rathaus
sights.content: This is one of the finest in Europe and has been included on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Building work started in 1410 and it is seen as an important display of the wealth and freedom of the city.

sights.name: Roland
sights.content: This statue on the main square, in front of the town hall, is of the Knight Roland, subject of the Medieval epic, the Song of Roland, who was a protector of trade. He appears in many European cities, especially those involved in the Hanseat

sights.name: Dom St. Petri
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 10:00–17:00, Sat 10:00–14:00, Sun 14:00–17:00 (Check website for tower hours)
sights.price: Free entry to cathedral; Tower and Museum: €3–5
sights.content: Over 1,200 years old, its huge towered façade dominates the main square. The interior is also impressive, with some fine painted details on the ceilings. The cathedral was damaged by fire and lightning in the 17th century and also seriously

sights.name: Böttcherstraße
sights.content: An incredible ''Jugendstil'' (Art Nouveau) street that runs from the main square towards the river. There are many fine façades and courtyards all with large amounts of design detail. There is an impressive Glockenspiel that chimes at regul

sights.name: Wallanlagen
sights.content: Built on the site of the former city fortifications, this star-shaped park is the oldest public garden in Germany. It features scenic walking paths, colorful flowerbeds, and the historic "Am Wall" windmill.

sights.name: Schnoor
sights.content: Bremen's oldest district, characterized by narrow lanes and timber-framed houses dating back to the 15th and 16th centuries. Once a quarter for fishermen and craftsmen, it now hosts numerous galleries, cafés, and small handicraft shops.

sights.name: Focke Museum
sights.price: permanent exhibition €6, children €2, and special exhibition €8, children €4
sights.content: A good overview of the history of Bremen City with a wide range of collections.

sights.name: Universum Science Center
sights.content: Science museum with plenty of interactive exhibits such as an earthquake simulator. The main building is a huge steel shell designed by the Bremen architect Thomas Klumpp.

sights.name: Hafenmuseum Speicher XI
sights.content: Housed in a former cotton warehouse. Models of ships used during the past.

sights.name: Gerhard-Marcks-Haus
sights.content: The contemporary art museum shows the work of [[w:Gerhard Marcks

sights.name: Wilhelm-Wagenfeld-Haus
sights.content: Founded as a design museum but also used for exhibitions in modern art. The museum is named after [[w:Wilhelm Wagenfeld

sights.name: Weserburg
sights.content: Modern art museum located on the Teerhof peninsula.

foodDrink.content: Grilled sausages

foodDrink.content: Spanish cuisine

foodDrink.name: Kiefert Imbiss
foodDrink.content: Grilled sausages

foodDrink.content: A Turkish eatery

foodDrink.name: Pyramide
foodDrink.content: Spanish and Syrian dishes

foodDrink.name: Bremer Ratskeller
foodDrink.content: Stunning classic wine cellar located in the basement of the historic city hall. Has stored and sold German wines since 1405. Large menu includes regional specialties and has English translations.

foodDrink.name: Gasthof zum Kaiser Friedrich
foodDrink.content: Slightly smoked cut of pork with cabbage and mashed potatoes (Braunkohlteller)

unescoSites: Town Hall and Roland on the Marketplace of Bremen

sights.name: Buxtehude Museum für Regionalgeschichte und Kunst

foodDrink.name: Amadeus
foodDrink.content: A lot of dishes are made in a stone oven. So you get here pizza, steak and burger.

foodDrink.name: Great Plains Steakhouse
foodDrink.content: Steakhouse. Make your salad as you wish at the salad bar and choose from their own made bread.

foodDrink.name: Fidelio - Bistro & Restaurant
foodDrink.content: You can find here schnitzel, burgers, pizza and pasta.

foodDrink.name: Süße Sünde
foodDrink.content: Frozen Yoghurt, Waffles, Pancakes and Cakes.

sights.name: Nagelsche Fachwerkhäuser
sights.content: Brick and timber houses built in 1659

foodDrink.name: Holstein Center
foodDrink.content: A shopping center

foodDrink.name: Ristorante La Grappa
foodDrink.content: Italian restaurant serving soups, salads, pizza and pasta. Value not only to tradition, but also fresh culinary ideas

foodDrink.name: Sabai Jai
foodDrink.hours: Mon-Sat noon-15ː00 and 17ː00-22ː00, Sun noon-22ː00, Tue closed
foodDrink.content: Traditional Thai restaurant

sights.name: St. Marien
sights.hours: Mon-Sat 10:00-17:00 Sun 13:00-17:00; The church will be closed for renovation work from 2 November 2026 until expected May 2027
sights.content: The largest church in Lübeck, and a key example of brick Gothic architecture. Built between 1277 and 1351, it features the highest brick vault in the world.

sights.name: The Dom
sights.content: Founded in 1173 by Henry the Lion, this is one of the oldest monuments in Lübeck and the first large brick church built on the Baltic coast. Initially constructed as a Romanesque basilica and later converted into a Gothic hall church, it is

sights.name: St. Petri
sights.content: Its tower platform (which can be reached by an elevator) offers a great view over the city, and if weather conditions allow it you can even see Travemünde (17 km to the north-east).

sights.name: St. Jakobi
sights.content: This 14th-century seafarers' church survived World War II intact, preserving its original historic interior. It is known for its historic pipe organs and a memorial chapel dedicated to the lost sailing ship ''Pamir''.

sights.name: St. Aegidien
sights.content: The smallest of Lübeck's five medieval parish churches was spared from destruction in World War II. Its interior combines medieval frescoes with a carved 1587 Renaissance singers' gallery and a prominent Baroque altar.

sights.name: St. Katharinen
sights.content: This early 14th-century former Franciscan monastery church is the only surviving conventual church in Lübeck's Old Town. Today operating as a museum, it features an elevated choir built over a double-nave crypt and exterior sculptures by Er

sights.name: Holstentor
sights.content: Being featured on the pre-reunification 50-mark banknote, this gate is easily the most recognised landmark of Lübeck in Germany. The gate nowadays hosts a museum.

sights.name: Behnhaus/Drägerhaus
sights.content: A Classicist burgher house that now hosts an art museum.

sights.name: Rathaus
sights.content: Its architecture is a stylistic potpourri reaching back to the 12th century. It is still the seat of the city administration and not a museum, so you can't have a look inside on your own. But there are guided tours every hour or so where th

sights.name: Willy Brandt House
sights.content: Dedicated to the former chancellor (1969-1974) and leader of the Social Democratic Party who was born in Lübeck in 1912.

sights.name: Haus der Kaufmannschaft
sights.content: A building built by the wealthy merchants.

sights.name: Buddenbrookhaus
sights.content: Dedicated to the brothers Thomas and Heinrich Mann, who spent their youth there. It contains many of their works. Closed until 2023.

sights.name: Günter-Grass-Haus
sights.content: Dedicated to the author (born in Gdańsk) who spent most of his life in Lübeck until his death in 2015 and who received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1999.

sights.name: Museumshafen
sights.content: It features some old-fashioned ships, among them a rebuilt Hanseatic ''kraweel'' ("Lisa von Lübeck") — more so in winter, because many of these ships are still in use during summer.

sights.name: European Hansemuseum
sights.price: €16 for adults in main exhibition, reduced price €10, free for children (under 18), university students
sights.content: Opened in 2015, this is perhaps the "crown jewel" among Lübeck's historical museums as it gives an in-depth look into Lübeck's over 800 years of history and how Lübeck shaped the Hanseatic League and how the ''Hanse'' in turn shaped Lübeck.

sights.name: Industriemuseum Geschichtswerkstatt Herrenwyk
sights.content: Dedicated to the [[Industrial tourism

sights.name: Grenz-Dokumentationsstätte Lübeck-Schlutup
sights.content: As Lübeck's eastern border was co-extensive with the border between West (FRG) and East Germany (GDR) during the [[Cold War Europe

sights.name: Theaterfigurenmuseum Lübeck
sights.content: A museum dedicated to all kinds of theatre puppets.

sights.name: Museum für Natur und Umwelt Lübeck
sights.content: A natural history museum featuring, among other things, an entire sperm whale skeleton taken from an unlucky whale that died in a beaching incident.

foodDrink.name: My hummus
foodDrink.content: Vegetarian cuisine.

foodDrink.name: Kartoffelspeicher
foodDrink.content: Restaurant specializing in potato dishes.

foodDrink.name: Bei Ulla
foodDrink.content: German cuisine. The restaurant has been in existence since 1967. Homemade dishes.

foodDrink.name: Das Flammkuchenhaus
foodDrink.content: An Alsace restaurant.

foodDrink.name: La Vigna
foodDrink.content: It is a small Italian café in the middle of the old town of Lübeck.

foodDrink.name: Taste
foodDrink.content: Bagels, fresh juices, soups and other tasty things with many vegetarian options

foodDrink.name: Marae
foodDrink.content: Vegan restaurant with homemade lemonade and raw cakes.

foodDrink.name: Restaurant Korfu
foodDrink.content: Greek food.

foodDrink.name: Neue Rösterei
foodDrink.content: They roast their own coffee.

foodDrink.name: NUI to go – Sushibar
foodDrink.content: A sushi place also offering Thai food.

foodDrink.name: Schiffergesellschaft
foodDrink.content: Excellent food in historic building. Good friendly service (a lot of staff). Many rooms, but if you want a seat in the main hall a reservation is recommended. Prices are a little higher than some but well worth it for the quality of the foo

foodDrink.name: Treibsand
foodDrink.content: A music venue run by volunteers of a leftish/alternative bend. Prices are moderate as they only charge enough to cover costs.

foodDrink.name: Cafe Brazil
foodDrink.content: Run by volunteers of a leftish/alternative bent.

guideSights.name: Hauptkirche St. Michaelis
guideSights.note: The youngest and most famous of the five is also the only baroque church. This building is not the original St. Michaelis - that one (built 1647-1669) was destroyed by a lightning strike in 1750. It was not until 1786 that the present churc

guideSights.name: Hauptkirche St. Jacobi
guideSights.note: St. Jacobi has been a parish since the 12th century, when it was not even within Hamburg's then city walls. The present-day church is a reconstruction of the late medieval one from the 15th century, which was destroyed during the Second Wor

guideSights.name: Hauptkirche St. Petri
guideSights.note: St. Petri was a cathedral as early as the 12th century or possibly even earlier. As with other ''Hauptkirchen'', the present version is one of many successive, and was only completed in 1878 after the great fire in 1842 consumed its predece

guideSights.name: Hauptkirche St. Nikolai
guideSights.note: All five main churches of Hamburg were damaged in World War II. But in contrast to the other four, St. Nikolai has not been re-erected making it a memorial against war. It was designed by English architect George Gilbert Scott. The steeple

guideSights.name: Hauptkirche St. Katharinen
guideSights.note: Situated on an island, it traditionally served as the church of the seamen. The base of its spire, dating from the 13th century, is the second oldest building preserved in the city. The church is also famous for its centuries-old organ, pla

guideSights.name: Hulbe-Haus
guideSights.note: Dating from the beginning of the 20th century as most buildings around, but looking much older.

guideSights.name: Radio Hamburg
guideSights.note: Under the building you can visit the remains of the bishops tower, from the 11th century. On the other side of the road, you can see excavations in progress, seeking the remains of the small fortress Hammaburg, which was erected in the 9th

guideSights.name: Rathaus
guideSights.note: Hamburg's impressive city hall was built in 1897 out of sandstone in neo-Renaissance style, including a 112-m tower. The square in front of the city hall is the Rathausmarkt, hosting many events especially in summer. Inside there are severa

guideSights.name: Hamburger Börse
guideSights.note: Between the buildings, there is a little courtyard called Rathaushof with its fountain, Hygieia-Brunnen.

guideSights.name: Wall-Anlagen
guideSights.note: The western part of the former city wall is nowadays a park area surrounding the inner city as a semicircle, ranging from the Landungsbrücken (Helgoländer Allee) up to Binnenalster. In the Wallanlagen there's a big playground and in the win

guideSights.name: Patriotische Gesellschaft
guideSights.note: The building of the Patriotic Society was erected following the great fire of 1842 on the former site of the old town hall of Hamburg. Built using the most modern technology at that time, including concrete substructure, and featuring moder

guideSights.name: Trostbrücke
guideSights.note: It has statues of Graf Adolf III and Bishop Ansgar on both sides.

guideSights.name: Zollenbrücke
guideSights.note: Hamburg's oldest remaining bridge from the 17th century

guideSights.name: Hopfenmarkt
guideSights.note: The hop market with its fountain Vierländerinbrunnen

guideSights.name: Alte Deichstraße
guideSights.note: Ensemble of traditional half-timbered merchant houses.

guideSights.name: Nicolai Fleet
guideSights.note: This is the site where Hamburg's harbour was some centuries ago.

guideSights.name: Kleiner Michel
guideSights.note: Built after the reformation, it's functioned as a Catholic church since the 19th century.

guideSights.name: The Miniatur Wunderland
guideSights.note: The world's largest model railway layout. The panoramas include parts of Hamburg, the Alps, the American west, South America, and a Scandinavian exhibit which features automated ships on a body of water. It also has an airport exhibit with

guideSights.name: Viewpoint towards the water castle
guideSights.note: One of the more famous photo spots in Hamburg on Poggenmühle bridge.

guideSights.name: visitor's centre
guideSights.note: New 'architectural lighthouse' of Hamburg. On the top of a huge old warehouse a 110 metres tall modern philharmonic hall with glass façade and wave-shaped roof. It also includes a fancy hotel, restaurant, as well as private apartments. Acce

guideSights.name: HafenCity Kesselhaus InfoCenter
guideSights.note: Here you can find information about the new buildings and the whole district. The InfoCenter also provides free guided tours.

guideSights.name: HafenCity View Point
guideSights.note: Look at the erecting process from an orange observation tower, which allows nice views on the HafenCity, the harbour, and the river.

guideSights.name: City und Sportboothafen
guideSights.note: Hamburg's city and yacht harbour.

guideSights.name: Feuerschiff LV 13
guideSights.note: The big red lighthouse ship hosts a restaurant today.

guideSights.name: Überseebrücke
guideSights.note: This is where big cruise liners used to dock when coming to Hamburg.

guideSights.name: Krameramtswohnungen
guideSights.note: The shopkeeper-office-flats are the last example of a typical 17th-century housing estate.

guideSights.name: Flussschifferkirche
guideSights.note: Germany's only floating church in Rothenburgsort.

guideSights.name: Portugiesenviertel
guideSights.note: Especially during the warmer months the area around Ditmar-Koel-Straße has a very special flair. Lots of restaurants and shops invite one to linger.

guideSights.name: Kunsthalle
guideSights.note: Glockengießerwall north of Hauptbahnhof. The museum houses an important collection of paintings from the 19th century with works from Max Liebermann, Lovis Corinth, Philipp Otto Runge, Caspar David Friedrich, Adolf Menzel, and modern arts.

guideSights.name: Deichtorhallen
guideSights.note: The Deichtorhallen is one of the best known exhibition galleries worldwide. The historical buildings are divided into an exhibition hall for contemporary art and the "House of Photography". Together the two buildings organize a highly diver

guideSights.name: Hamburg Museum
guideSights.note: Holstenwall, close to Underground station "St. Pauli". This is the museum of city history, bringing the past to life with a lot of models showing the development of the harbour and the city. The club "MEHEV" is showing a 40-year-old and one

guideSights.name: Speicherstadtmuseum
guideSights.note: Branch of Museum of Labour in docklands warehouse. History of the district and tea and coffee trade.

guideSights.name: Cap San Diego
guideSights.note: One of the last generation of pre-containerisation cargo ships (built in the 1960s), now semi-permanently moored halfway between Landungsbrücken and the Speicherstadt, and is the largest functional cargo museum ship in the world. The ship h

guideSights.name: Automuseum Prototyp
guideSights.note: Museum of car prototypes, nice shop inside.

guideSights.name: Spicey's Gewürzmuseum
guideSights.note: Located in the Speicherstadt. They claim to be the world's only spice museum.

guideSights.name: Chocoversum Hachez Schokoladen-Museum
guideSights.note: The Chocoversum is a "museum" run by chocolate manufacturer Hachez from Hamburg's fellow ''Hansestadt'' Bremen. Rather than focus on exhibiting historic artifacts, it presents the process of making chocolate from the plantation up to the fi

guideSights.name: Rickmer Rickmers
guideSights.note: A museum sailing ship (three-masted bark) from 1896, permanently moored off the Landungsbrücken. On board is a museum, a small restaurant, and an escape room.

guideSights.name: Dialog im Dunkeln
guideSights.note: Sighted people get to experience the everyday life of blind people. In completely dark rooms blind people guide the sighted through the exhibition.

guideSights.name: Altonaer Museum
guideSights.note: Dedicated to Altona's, Hamburg's and northern Germany's cultural history.

guideSights.name: Altona City Hall
guideSights.note: Built in 1898, when Altona was still a separate city. It's an impressive building with influences of Italian Renaissance.

guideSights.name: Dockland
guideSights.note: Walk 136 steps to the roof of this building to get a wonderful view of the harbour. The six-storey glass and steel building has the shape of a parallelogram and is reminiscent of a ship bow.

guideSights.name: Altonaer Volkspark
guideSights.note: This used to be the city park of the independent town of Altona. Unlike Hamburger Stadtpark, this park has been left in a more natural state. On the northern edge of the park is Volksparkstadion, the home stadium of the football team HSV, a

guideSights.name: Landungsbrücken
guideSights.note: The most touristy part of Hamburg's harbour, close to the metro station with the same name. Piers connected with several bridges swim on the water adapting to the tide. There tourist boats land and you will find souvenir shops, restaurants,

guideSights.name: U-434
guideSights.note: One of the biggest non-nuclear Soviet submarines, moored near to the Fischmarkt. Guided tours are possible.

guideSights.name: Alter Elbtunnel
guideSights.note: Completed in 1911, it links both sides of the river Elbe. A lift or stairs bring you the 24 m down into the tunnel. You then walk through one of its two 427-m-long pipes having 12 m of water over your head. At the other side, you again walk

guideSights.name: Museumshafen Oevelgönne
guideSights.note: Historical boats.

guideSights.name: Hamburger Dom
guideSights.note: A large fair held at Heiligengeistfeld fair ground. With three fairs (spring, summer and winter) per year it is the biggest and the longest fair throughout Germany and attracts every one approximately ten million visitors per year.

guideSights.name: Reeperbahn
guideSights.note: A street and entertainment district in Hamburg's St. Pauli district, one of the two centres of Hamburg's nightlife (with [[Hamburg/Altona-St._Pauli#Schanzenviertel

guideSights.name: Panoptikum
guideSights.note: A wax cabinet with a history of over 125 years and as such the oldest in Germany, though it has been in its current location since the 1950s. Not as big and famous as Madame Tussauds in London, nevertheless the figures have been created wit

guideSights.name: Flakturm IV
guideSights.note: Right at the Heiligengeistfeld is a World War II bunker, visible from far away due to its size. Nowadays the building houses different media companies and agentures, and there's a dance club on the upper floor.

guideSights.name: St. Pauli Archiv
guideSights.note: Archive for the city district and history workshop. Arranges very interesting themed walks around St. Pauli.

guideSights.name: Hafenstraße
guideSights.note: The street was a place for squatters in the 1980s and was well known by the media when there were "battles" between the Autonomous movement and the police. Some squats still exist there, though the "80s-Myth" is dead. You can go to the Punk

guideSights.name: Beatles-Platz
guideSights.note: There is a sculpture honouring the Beatles. Also in the Reeperbahn area are clubs where the Beatles played at various times from 1960 to 1962, including the Indra club and Star Club.

guideSights.name: Grosse Freiheit
guideSights.note: In the pedestrian street there are a lot of bars and clubs - a great place to go in the evening, although it's very crowded and it may get a bit dangerous in the weekend. On weekdays, it is harmless here - a low-budget tip is, 99 Cent Bar,

guideSights.name: Hans-Albers-Platz
guideSights.note: Between Reeperbahn and Herbertstraße there's a memorial for an actor who was advertising the Kiez (Reeperbahn). Especially the movie ''Große Freiheit Nummer 7'' helped making the Kiez famous.

guideSights.name: Herbertstraße
guideSights.note: The epicenter of the red-light district, this short street runs parallel to Reeperbahn is closed off by gates from both ends. Adults only and photography is strictly banned.

guideSights.name: Spielbudenplatz
guideSights.note: The place got its name from the entertainers putting up shows here for sailors from all over the world back in the day. For example Mr. Hagenback (who opened the zoo park in the city) showcased his sea lions here. Today it is surrounded by

guideSights.name: Rote Flora
guideSights.note: This building used to be the last squatted house in Hamburg, it's now left to the squatters for free by the owner. During the week, it is turned into a café, concerts of various styles or other events may also take place. On some days there

guideSights.name: Christianskirche
guideSights.note: Baroque church in Ottensen.

guideSights.name: Zeise Hallen
guideSights.note: The halls were built in 1857 for the Zeise company manufacturing ship parts. The company went bust in 1979, and nowadays the cultural heritage building is used as a cultural center with a movie theater.

guideSights.name: Planten un Blomen
guideSights.note: This park is partially on the old city wall of Hamburg. Already in the 1930s the former zoological park was remodeled into a bird and entertainment park for the Lower German Garden Exhibition (Niederdeutsche Gartenschau). Afterwards it was

guideSights.name: Jenisch park
guideSights.note: The oldest landscaped park in Hamburg. Two museums, Jenisch House and Ernst Barlach House, are in the park. Flottbek River flows through the park and into the Elbe at Teufelsbrück.

guideSights.name: Baurs Park
guideSights.note: Nice park with views to the Elbe river.

guideSights.name: Loki Schmidt Garten
guideSights.note: For a century and a half, the botanical garden was situated in the current Planten un Blomen park, where the tropical greenhouses still remain. In 1979, the botanical garden was relocated to its current place in the Klein Flottbek district.

guideSights.name: Hamburg Stadtpark
guideSights.note: 150 ha of park with a pretty good Planetarium at an old water tower in its middle, multiple sporting areas and boat rental on the lake.

guideSights.name: Alsterpark
guideSights.note: Inaugurated in 1952. The part west of the Alster is called ''Alstervorland'', the one east ''Alterpark''.

guideSights.name: Eimsbüttler Park
guideSights.note: This former forest and current park has survived both world wars and still offers green pastures around the Weiher lake together with a playground, swimming pool and a café.

guideSights.name: Friedhof Ohlsdorf
guideSights.note: One of the world's biggest graveyards.

guideSights.name: Imam-Ali-Mosque
guideSights.note: Biggest of all mosques in Hamburg. Centre of the religious and cultural life of the huge Iranian community. The Imams of Hamburg happen to have played important roles in Iran's religious and political everyday life since their installation

guideSights.name: Museum am Rothenbaum - Kulturen und Kunste der Welt
guideSights.note: Formerly known as the Museum of Ethnology. The museum has ethnographic objects from around the world.

guideSights.name: Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe
guideSights.note: The museum is a leading centre for art, applied art, and design. Its collections of work from Europe and the Middle and the Far East are of the finest-quality and span all epochs from the Ancient World to the present day. They also have man

guideSights.name: Dreieinigkeitskirche St. Georg
guideSights.note: Baroque church in Sankt Georg.

guideSights.name: St.-Marien-Dom St. Georg
guideSights.note: Since 1995, this neo-romanesque church is the cathedral of the youngest Roman Catholic archbishop of Germany. Though the church has not the splendor one might expect, next to it you may find the first statue world wide of the late pope, Joh

guideSights.name: Memorial to the X-ray martyrs of the world
guideSights.note: This monument is devoted to researchers, physicians, physicists, radiographers, laboratory technicians and nurses who died from injuries or illnesses caused by prolonged exposure to radiation used in medicine. On the list of about 360 names

guideSights.name: St. Pankratius
guideSights.note: This 17th-century church features carvings depicting scenes from the Old and New Testaments, and an organ by the famous organ builder Arp Schnitger.

guideSights.name: Container port
guideSights.note: Hamburg's massive container ports line the southern bank of the river Elbe. They are most spectacular at night, and the best place to view them from is by driving north along the A7 highway (heading into the Elbtunnel tunnel). They are not

guideSights.name: Aussichtspunkt Steinwerder
guideSights.note: A viewing platform at the southern end of the Alter Elbtunnel, with great views on Landungsbrücken, the Elbphilharmonie, and Hamburg's harbourfront.

guideSights.name: Pfarrkirche St. Pankratius in Neuenfelde
guideSights.note: 17th century church, famous for the biggest organ Arp Schnitger built.

guideSights.name: BallinStadt Auswanderwelt Hamburg
guideSights.note: It was built in 1892 under the guidance of Albert Ballin to provide medical care and accommodation to migrants, who were emigrating to the United States on HAPAG ships. The complex was converted into a museum, though its original design and

guideSights.name: Archaeological Museum Hamburg
guideSights.note: Museum presenting prehistorical and early historical northern Germany as well as the history of the city of Harburg.

guideSights.name: Sammlung Falckenberg
guideSights.note: The Falckenberg Collection of the Cultural Foundation Phönix Art is a notable collection of modern art. Public tours Saturday on afternoons, you can also visit other times by calling ahead.
